title: A memory leak appears after opening and closing a modal repeatedly
description: Problem: A memory leak appears after opening and closing a modal repeatedly. Solve this problem with multiple approaches and detailed explanations.

data.text: Users open a confirmation modal, close it, and repeat this dozens of times. After a while the tab uses more memory than expected, animations stutter, and eventually the browser crashes the tab. In a single-page application this usually means the modal or something inside it is retaining references after it unmounts.

items: Event listeners attached to window, document, or a portal root without cleanup in useEffect.
setInterval or setTimeout callbacks that keep running after the component unmounts.
Closures capturing large objects and being stored in a global or module-level variable.
Third-party widgets or rich-text editors that create DOM nodes and never remove them.
RxJS subscriptions or WebSocket connections left open after modal close.
React state or refs in a parent that accumulate arrays or maps on every open/close cycle.

terms.definition: The process by which the JavaScript engine reclaims memory from objects that are no longer reachable.
The total memory kept alive by a single object because it references other objects that would otherwise be collectible.
A reference to an object that does not prevent garbage collection, useful for caches and mappings.
A DevTools view of the JavaScript heap that shows which objects are alive and what references keep them alive.

data.text: Use Chrome DevTools Memory panel. Take a heap snapshot before opening the modal, then open and close the modal ten times, then take another snapshot. If the retained size of the modal, its listeners, or any closure grows linearly, you have a leak. The Comparison view makes it easy to spot objects that were allocated but never collected.

data.title: Use AbortController for fetch and timers
data.text: For fetch, timers, and subscriptions, pass an AbortSignal or track a mounted flag. The cleanup function should abort in-flight work so callbacks never fire after unmount.

data.definition:
graph TD
    A[User opens modal] --> B[Mount modal component]
    B --> C[Attach listeners / timers / subscriptions]
    C --> D[User interacts]
    D --> E[User closes modal]
    E --> F[Unmount modal component]
    F --> G[Run cleanup function]
    G --> H[Remove listeners / clear timers / close subscriptions]
    H --> I[Objects become unreachable]
    I --> J[Garbage collector reclaims memory]
    J --> K[Heap size returns to baseline]

items.question: Why does the leak happen only after opening and closing repeatedly?
items.answer: Each open/close cycle allocates new listeners, closures, or DOM nodes. One cycle is harmless. Dozens of cycles accumulate until the heap grows enough to trigger GC pressure or tab termination.

items.question: Could React itself be holding the memory?
items.answer: React releases component state when a component unmounts, but only if nothing external is still referencing that state. Event listeners on window or module-level caches are common external retainers.

items.question: Should I use WeakMap to store modal state?
items.answer: WeakMap helps when you need a cache that does not prevent garbage collection. It does not fix leaks caused by lingering event listeners or closures. Fix the cleanup first, then consider WeakMap for caches.

data.title: Find and fix a memory leak
data.description: Use DevTools to confirm a leak in a modal pattern, then fix the cleanup.
steps: Open a page with a modal that opens and closes.
Open Memory panel and take a heap snapshot.
Open and close the modal twenty times.
Take another heap snapshot and compare.
Identify the object type or closure retaining memory and add cleanup.
data.expectedOutcome: After the fix, repeated open/close cycles should not increase retained heap size, and the detached DOM tree count should stay near zero.

data.title: Summary
points: Memory leaks in modals are usually missing cleanup for listeners, timers, or subscriptions.
Use heap snapshots to confirm the leak and identify the retaining path.
Always return a cleanup function from useEffect.
Use AbortController for fetch and timers so work stops on unmount.
Validate the fix by repeating the user flow and comparing heap sizes
data.takeaway: Cleanup is not optional in interactive components. A modal that works once but leaks on repeated use will eventually degrade the entire application for every user.
